findings.requirement: Anthropic Messages API specification & Decision E1/E2/E8: valid message turn alternation and role ordering
findings.finding: AnthropicClient._convert forwards consecutive user or assistant messages directly to the Anthropic API without merging or validation whenever history contains consecutive turns, ends in a user turn, or begins with an assistant turn, causing Anthropic to reject the request with HTTP 400.
findings.evidence: Calling AnthropicClient._convert([ChatMessage(role='user', content='u1'), ChatMessage(role='user', content='u2')]) produces (None, [{'role': 'user', 'content': 'u1'}, {'role': 'user', 'content': 'u2'}]). In AgenticOrchestrator.run (line 239), user_message is appended after history, so any history ending in a user turn guarantees consecutive user messages sent to Anthropic.
findings.reproduce: .venv/bin/python -c 'from hrms_plugin.ai.llm import AnthropicClient, ChatMessage; print(AnthropicClient._convert([ChatMessage(role="user", content="u1"), ChatMessage(role="user", content="u2")]))'

findings.requirement: Anthropic Messages API specification & Decision E8: non-empty content strings in message turns
findings.finding: HistoryItem allows empty content strings because Field(max_length=32000) lacks min_length=1, resulting in either empty string user blocks or dropped assistant turns that cause Anthropic API 400 errors.
findings.evidence: In hrms_plugin/server/app.py:97, content: str = Field(max_length=32000) accepts ''. In hrms_plugin/ai/llm.py:533-538, an empty assistant content string results in content = [], failing if content: and dropping the turn, which causes adjacent user turns to collide into consecutive user messages.
findings.reproduce: .venv/bin/python -c 'from hrms_plugin.ai.llm import AnthropicClient, ChatMessage; print(AnthropicClient._convert([ChatMessage(role="user", content="u1"), ChatMessage(role="assistant", content=""), ChatMessage(role="user", content="u2")]))'

findings.requirement: Anthropic Messages API specification: tool_result blocks must match preceding assistant tool_use blocks
findings.finding: AnthropicClient._convert does not verify that tool messages are preceded by a matching assistant tool_use block, creating orphaned tool_result blocks in consecutive user messages that fail Anthropic API validation.
findings.evidence: In hrms_plugin/ai/llm.py:517-528, when a tool message follows a user message, _convert appends {'role': 'user', 'content': [{'type': 'tool_result', ...}]}, creating two consecutive user turns with an orphaned tool_result.
findings.reproduce: .venv/bin/python -c 'from hrms_plugin.ai.llm import AnthropicClient, ChatMessage; print(AnthropicClient._convert([ChatMessage(role="user", content="q"), ChatMessage(role="tool", content="{}", tool_call_id="call_x")]))'

findings.requirement: Decision E7: retries on 429/5xx honouring Retry-After with exponential backoff
findings.finding: _retry_delay fails to parse RFC 7231 / RFC 9110 HTTP-date Retry-After headers, prematurely falling back to exponential backoff, and fails to guard against NaN delay values.
findings.evidence: In hrms_plugin/ai/llm.py:168-176, float(retry_after) raises ValueError on standard HTTP-dates (e.g. 'Wed, 21 Oct 2026 07:28:00 GMT'), which is silently caught and ignored by except ValueError: pass, while 'nan' yields delay nan.
findings.reproduce: .venv/bin/python -c 'import httpx; from hrms_plugin.ai.llm import _retry_delay; r = httpx.Response(429, headers={"retry-after": "Wed, 21 Oct 2026 07:28:00 GMT"}); print(_retry_delay(r, 0))'

findings.requirement: Decision E7: OpenAI-compatible and Gemini clients each reuse one httpx.AsyncClient
findings.finding: MappingSynthesizer.synthesize_agentic creates a new LLMGateway and httpx.AsyncClient on every invocation without cleanup lifecycle methods, leaking client connections and SSL contexts.
findings.evidence: In hrms_plugin/schema/synthesizer.py:798, gateway = llm_gateway or LLMGateway() creates a new LLMGateway instance each call. In hrms_plugin/ai/llm.py:385 and 606, OpenAICompatibleClient and GeminiClient instantiate a new httpx.AsyncClient with no close() or aclose() methods anywhere in llm.py.
findings.reproduce: .venv/bin/python -c 'from hrms_plugin.ai.llm import LLMGateway, LLMConfig, LLMProvider; g1 = LLMGateway(LLMConfig(provider=LLMProvider.OPENAI)); g2 = LLMGateway(LLMConfig(provider=LLMProvider.OPENAI)); print(g1.client._http is not g2.client._http, hasattr(g1, "aclose"))'

findings.requirement: Decision E8 / Problem E-P7: ChatRequest.history support across chat endpoints
findings.finding: ChatRequest.history is completely ignored and dropped by /v1/chat/stream, depriving streaming conversations of prior context.
findings.evidence: In hrms_plugin/server/app.py:200, agent.stream_agentic is invoked with only message, jurisdiction, context, and auth. Neither SupervisorAgent.stream_agentic (supervisor.py:631) nor AgenticOrchestrator.run_stream (orchestrator.py:267) accepts a history parameter, and orchestrator.py:284-287 hardcodes messages to only system and current user turns.

findings.requirement: Decision E6: unconfigured LLM maps to HTTP 503 {'error': 'LLM_NOT_CONFIGURED'}
findings.finding: /v1/chat/stream returns HTTP 200 instead of HTTP 503 when the LLM is unconfigured, emitting an in-band SSE error event because StreamingResponse commits HTTP 200 before checking configuration.
findings.evidence: In hrms_plugin/server/app.py:214, chat_stream_endpoint returns StreamingResponse(event_generator(), ...), committing HTTP 200 OK headers immediately. When LLMNotConfigured is raised inside event_generator(), line 208 yields an SSE error event instead of responding with HTTP 503 as specified by Decision E6.
findings.reproduce: POST to /v1/chat/stream with LLM_PROVIDER=bard returns HTTP status 200 with SSE payload 'data: {"event": "error", "data": {"error": "LLM_NOT_CONFIGURED"}}\n\n'.

findings.requirement: Test Table E3 / Decision E3: orchestrator refusal handling verification
findings.finding: Tests test_refusal_is_returned_and_no_tool_runs and test_refusal_after_a_tool_ran are vacuous tests that would pass even if refusal handling were removed, because AgenticOrchestrator contains no refusal-specific logic.
findings.evidence: In hrms_plugin/agents/orchestrator.py:251-253, any LLMResponse with empty tool_calls returns reply_text and confidence 0.98 unconditionally. The word 'refusal' does not exist in orchestrator.py, confirmed by git grep.
findings.reproduce: git grep -n 'refusal' hrms_plugin/agents/orchestrator.py exits with code 1.

findings.requirement: Test Table E7 / Decision E7: verify one HTTP client is reused across calls
findings.finding: test_one_http_client_is_reused vacuously passes by checking an explicitly pre-injected client parameter on the instance attribute rather than testing client lifecycle or gateway reuse.
findings.evidence: In tests/unit/test_llm_providers.py:252-255 and 292-298, the test explicitly passes a mock http_client to OpenAICompatibleClient and asserts client._http is first, verifying only Python attribute assignment rather than gateway reuse or default client lifecycle.

findings.requirement: Decision E1: any invalid effort value raises LLMNotConfigured
findings.finding: LLMConfig and AnthropicClient do not validate effort during instantiation, allowing invalid effort levels to bypass validation when not loaded from environment variables.
findings.evidence: In hrms_plugin/ai/llm.py:141, LLMConfig.effort has no validation. In llm.py:502, AnthropicClient.__init__ does not validate config.effort. Instantiating AnthropicClient(LLMConfig(effort='bogus')) succeeds and sends {'output_config': {'effort': 'bogus'}}.
findings.reproduce: .venv/bin/python -c 'from hrms_plugin.ai.llm import AnthropicClient, LLMConfig, LLMProvider; c = AnthropicClient(LLMConfig(provider=LLMProvider.ANTHROPIC, effort="bogus")); print(c.config.effort)'

findings.requirement: Decision E4: run_stream streams response text as token events
findings.finding: run_stream emits the complete response text in a single token event when no tool calls occur, defeating the user experience purpose of incremental token streaming.
findings.evidence: In hrms_plugin/agents/orchestrator.py:296-297, if llm_resp.content: yield {'event': 'token', 'data': llm_resp.content} sends the entire string as a single SSE event, unlike FakeLLMClient.chat_stream which yields incrementally word by word.
